en.title: Fewest Connected Blocks After Adding One Interval
en.description:
You are given closed intervals and may add exactly one extra closed interval with length b−a≤k. Find the minimum number of connected blocks after merging. Touching at the same endpoint counts as connected; intervals that differ by 1 are not automatically connected.

The input/output protocol and the explicitly marked supplementary constraints were compiled by this site; upstream solutions are not executed.
en.input: The first line contains n k, followed by n lines of a b. 1≤n≤200000, 1≤a≤b≤10⁹, 1≤k≤10⁹. The added interval may have length 0.
en.output: Output the single integer required by the problem.
en.explanation: The answers to the three public examples are, in order: 2; 1; 1. The examples were rechecked by independent enumeration, state search, or direct simulation.
hints: First sort and merge the existing intersecting intervals, then use two pointers to find the largest run of consecutive blocks that one segment can connect: the start of block r minus the end of block l is ≤k. Connecting w blocks reduces the total number of blocks by w−1.
